extracted.intended_audience: CIHR applicants, CIHR peer reviewers, funding agency staff, and research evaluators involved in CIHR grant programs
extracted.subtask_short: research assessment for CIHR peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for responsible research assessment used in CIHR program design, applications, and peer review — emphasizing holistic evaluation of diverse research contributions, mitigation of bias, and alignment with DORA and Tri-Agency narrative CV practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and value a range of research contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR recognizes and values a range of research contributions that can lead to impact; applications should encourage the inclusion of a broad range of contributions, from publications to societal outputs, in the Most Significant Contributions section of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Most Significant Contributions section and the Tri-Agency narrative CV to demonstrate diverse outputs and the research narrative. Examples include societal outputs, policy influence, datasets, software and other non-traditional outputs. This supports holistic assessment of a researcher's work based on its own merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use journal-based metrics as a surrogate measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use journal-based metrics, such as Journal Impact Factors, as a surrogate measure of the quality of individual research articles, to assess an individual scientist's contributions, or in hiring, promotion, or funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on journal prestige or single quantitative indicators when judging individual articles or applicants. CIHR's guidance and DORA recommend assessing scientific content directly rather than relying on metrics like JIF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on quantitative indicators; focus on quality over quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review guidelines ask reviewers to consider a greater variety of contributions, avoid relying on quantitative indicators, and focus on quality over quantity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize description and assessment of the quality, significance and influence of work rather than counting publications or citations. Use narrative sections (Most Significant Contributions, narrative CV) to explain importance rather than raw counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the applicant's context (career stage, leave history)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should consider the applicant's context (e.g., career stage, leave history).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess contributions in light of individual circumstances; use narrative CV elements such as career trajectory and mentorship roles to contextualize productivity and impact, especially for early-stage investigators or those with non-linear careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about evaluation criteria (for funding agencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about the criteria used in evaluating the scientific productivity of grant applications and clearly highlight, especially for early-stage investigators, that the scientific content of a paper is much more important than publication metrics or the identity of the journal in which it was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding agencies and programs should publish clear evaluation criteria so applicants and reviewers understand how productivity and impact are judged. Emphasize content over venue, and provide specific instructions for reviewing early-stage investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the value and impact of all research outputs including datasets and software
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of research assessment, consider the value and impact of all research outputs (including datasets and software) in addition to research publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include non-publication outputs in assessments and recognize diverse forms of scholarly contribution. Use qualitative indicators and narrative evidence to document impact of these outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider qualitative indicators of research impact (e.g., influence on policy and practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider a broad range of impact measures including qualitative indicators of research impact, such as influence on policy and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use descriptive evidence (case studies, policy citations, practice changes) and stakeholder testimony to document real-world impact rather than relying solely on quantitative metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical training and supports to reduce bias in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical training and supports for applicants and peer reviewers to reduce bias and support a fair process. Tri-agency Excellence in Peer and Merit Review learning modules include mandatory sections on DORA and bias mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require or offer training (e.g., 'Module 1: Biases in the Research Ecosystem' and 'Module 2: Mitigating Bias in the Peer and Merit Review Processes') for reviewers. Use these modules to raise awareness of metric-related bias and other systemic biases and to improve review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: When serving on committees, assess based on scientific content
rubrics_metrics.description: When involved in committees making decisions about funding, hiring, tenure, or promotion, make assessments based on scientific content rather than publication metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members should prioritize reading and evaluating the substance of outputs. Encourage practices that reward intellectual contribution and rigour; actively challenge reliance on venue or metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a range of article metrics and indicators on personal/supporting statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a range of article metrics and indicators on personal/supporting statements, as evidence of the impact of individual published articles and other research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow applicants to present multiple indicators (altmetrics, citation context, software downloads, dataset reuse) to support claims of impact, but interpret these indicators in context rather than as definitive measures of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite primary literature to give credit where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever appropriate, cite primary literature in which observations are first reported rather than reviews in order to give credit where credit is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage correct attribution practices in review and applicant materials so original contributions are properly recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote equity, diversity, inclusion and support for Indigenous research
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR and the tri-agencies have implemented policies that include support for Indigenous research and research training in Canada, and equity, diversity and inclusion considerations are integral to responsible research assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed EDI and culturally safe practices into assessment processes; ensure reviewers are aware of and apply these principles when evaluating proposals and contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for assessment that is inclusive, collaborative, transparent, culturally safe, and focused on real-world impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Excellence Framework positions CIHR toward a vision where Canadian health research is internationally recognized as inclusive, collaborative, transparent, culturally safe, and focused on real-world impact. Responsible research assessment is a key enabler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Framework as an overarching lens for program and review design. Strive for transparency in criteria and processes, inclusion of diverse perspectives, and emphasis on research that demonstrates tangible societal benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align reviews and assessment practices with DORA and international best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR is a signatory to DORA and committed to implementing its recommendations; reviewers and programs should align with DORA's guidance on improving research assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow DORA's six-step holistic approach where applicable, consult DORA resource library, and engage in international partnerships (e.g., Research on Research Institute) to adopt evidence-based improvements to assessment.
